content_voiceover: Treatment selection for mantle cell lymphoma hinges on two big questions, TP53 mutation status and whether the patient can tolerate aggressive therapy. For stage one or two nonbulky disease, or classical TP53 wildtype disease that's bulky stage two, three, or four, patients can receive either less aggressive or aggressive induction, depending on fitness. Less aggressive preferred options include acalabrutinib plus bendamustine rituximab followed by rituximab maintenance, acalabrutinib plus rituximab, or bendamustine rituximab alone. Aggressive induction for TP53 wildtype disease includes bendamustine rituximab followed by high dose cytarabine and rituximab, the LyMA regimen, the Nordic regimen with dose intensified maxi CHOP alternating with high dose cytarabine, or the TRIANGLE regimen, which alternates CHOP plus a covalent BTK inhibitor with DHAP style platinum based chemotherapy. Now here's the key distinction on the right: classical TP53 mutated disease, regardless of stage, is a different animal entirely. These patients respond poorly to intensive chemotherapy and transplant, so the guideline now recommends venetoclax and zanubrutinib plus obinutuzumab as suitable for all TP53 mutated patients, while the TRIANGLE regimen remains an option only for those fit enough for aggressive therapy, and acalabrutinib rituximab is explicitly called out as not suitable for TP53 mutated disease needing aggressive approaches.
keypoints: Treatment splits primarily on TP53 mutation status and patient fitness
TP53 wildtype: bendamustine rituximab, TRIANGLE, or Nordic regimen options
TP53 mutated disease responds poorly to intensive chemo and transplant
Venetoclax/zanubrutinib plus obinutuzumab is suitable for all TP53 mutated patients
TRIANGLE regimen combines CHOP/BTKi alternating with platinum-based DHAP chemotherapy
keypoint_voiceover: The exam pearl here is that TP53 mutation status now drives mantle cell lymphoma treatment selection as much as stage does, with TP53 mutated patients steered away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax, zanubrutinib, and obinutuzumab based regimens.
